newsitem.title: UK: Ethnic minorities at risk in Europe - Amnesty.
newsitem.headline: Ethnic minorities at risk in Europe - Amnesty.

text.p: Human rights group Amnesty International said on Wednesday that ethnic minorities were particularly at risk of torture, ill-treatment and police brutality in Europe.
In its annual report, the London-based group said the plight of European refugees also worsened last year.

Amnesty said "disappearances" took place in Bosnia and Turkey in 1996, adding that the fate of people who went missing in previous years in Bosnia, Cyprus, Croatia, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan remained unknown.
Torture or ill-treatment, including rape, took place in at least 33 European countries while prisoners of conscience were held in 17 countries.

In Bosnia, dozens of prisoners of conscience were detained on account of their nationality. Displaced people and refugees were prevented from returning home by violent attacks and damage to their houses, the report said.
The refugee crisis following the collapse of the former Yugoslavia in 1991 showed little sign of improvement, it added.
"Its (Europe's) worst human rights disaster since the 1940s is far from being resolved," Amnesty said.

"One year after the (Bosnia) peace agreement which brought an end to open conflict, there has been little real progress towards establishing the durably safe conditions which would allow refugees and displaced people to return to their homes."
In Russia there were numerous allegations of ethnic minorities being tortured in detention.
Allegations of police ill-treatment of foreigners were made in Germany and in Britain "a few deaths in custody took place in disputed circumstances", it said.
